text:
kim: Heads-up — planned maintenance Sat 2026-04-03 03:00 UTC for AZ3. We're doing a coordinated NIC firmware + interconnect cutover + staged GPU node reboots. Primary goal: reduce intermittent packet drops seen on saturn pool and validate ISP link failover.

alex: rough blast radius? how many nodes / queues?

kim: cohort size = ~20 GPU nodes (~1 rack). We'll do 4 cohorts to keep tail latency SLOs. Expect ~5-8% capacity hit during the window. No customer-facing API downtime expected w/ routing and fallbacks, but ML infra throughput will be reduced.

sam: timeline?

kim: high level: 
• 03:00 UTC: cohort A cordon & graceful drain (kv-cache prefix seed first)
• 03:10: NIC fw flash + BMC soft power cycle (infra-runner)
• 03:25: GPU node reboot -> kvcache reseed + perf sanity
• 03:40: cohort A back in service + probe sweep
• 04:00: cohort B starts (staggered every 40m)
(we expect full window ~3h)

maria: ops/cost note — if burst capacity kicks in for Hosted, we'll burn committed credits. Is there a plan to throttle non-prod?

kim: yes, plan includes: throttle non-prod tenants to 10% and route low-priority jobs to saturn-fallback-1 (us-east1) during cohorts. I'll post config snippets.

alex: can you paste the drain command we use? want to double-check hooks.

kim: here's the playbook excerpt: 
```
# cordon + drain with kvseed hook
kubectl cordon node/$NODE
redwoodctl drain --graceful --kv-seed --drain-timeout=600s --eviction-mode=best-effort
# infra-runner will push NIC FW and soft-power via BMC API
```

infra-bot: scheduled maintenance created: maintenance_id=mn-az3-20260403-01, start=2026-04-03T03:00:00Z, cohorts=4, owner=@kim

sam: any networking risk w/ ISP link cutover? last time we saw microbursts during BGP flap.

kim: good call — this cutover uses staged BGP flap with exponential backoff and traffic drain to fallback lanes. We'll keep egress QOS for high-priority tenants. ops-bot will trigger the link flip only after cohort cordon completes.

maria: can we add an automatic rollback if tail p50 latency > 120ms for more than 3min?

kim: yep. Rollback policy: if p50>120ms OR packetloss>0.5% across control probes for 3 continuous min -> abort flip + rebind traffic to original ISP and re-open cohort. infra-runner will annotate maintenance with rollback flags.

alex: what about Dedicated customers pinned to AZ3? they'll see capacity loss. ops to inform sales?

maria: I'll send a short comms to sales + CS with impacted pools and expected window. Also attaching cost estimate for burst credits: ~ $700/hr worst-case if we hit fallback.

kim: tagging @oncall in case we need manual intervention during the window. Please watch these dashboards: saturn-pool-latency, egress-qos, kvseed-success-rate.

ops-bot: @oncall reminder created for 2026-04-03T02:50Z. Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/az3-cutover

sam: I'll prep a canary; will inject small traffic after cohort A returns (simple gen + latency probe).

kim: thanks. final checklist before flip: 
- [ ] preflight nettrace collection (done)
- [ ] kvseed health check (green)
- [ ] non-prod throttle in place (maria)
- [ ] ops oncall scheduled (ops-bot)
- [ ] rollback policy set (kim)

alex: cool. i'll shadow cohort A ops. ping in thread when cohort A cordon starts.

kim: will do. pinging again ~30m prior with final go/no-go. :thermometer: :gear: :white_check_mark:
